title: Luria-Bertani (LB) Agar

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: A general-purpose solid medium widely used in molecular biology and recombinant DNA work for cultivating Escherichia coli and many other non-fastidious bacteria, commonly combined with antibiotics for plasmid selection.

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

compositionPerLiter.amount: 5-10 g (varies by Lennox vs. Miller formulation)

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

preparationSummary: Suspend the dehydrated powder (or combine components) in distilled/deionized water, heat with agitation to fully dissolve, sterilize, and cool to approximately 50°C before adding any heat-labile selective antibiotic and pouring plates.

sterilization.value: commonly autoclaved at 121°C for 15 minutes for typical batch volumes
sterilization.dependsOn: batch volume, container, and autoclave validation — not a universal setting for every load

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

storage: Store prepared plates refrigerated (commonly 2-8°C) in sealed bags to reduce dehydration, away from light; antibiotic-containing plates typically have a shorter usable shelf life than plain LB agar.

shelfLife.value: manufacturer-stated shelf life varies by product, and antibiotic-supplemented plates typically have a shorter usable life than plain plates
shelfLife.dependsOn: specific product, antibiotic added, and storage conditions

expectedAppearance: Pale amber, clear to slightly opalescent gel when properly prepared.
qualityControl: Confirm sterility (no growth on an uninoculated control plate) and, for antibiotic-supplemented plates, confirm that a known-resistant control strain grows and a known-sensitive strain does not before use in selection work.
manufacturerNotes: Exact salt concentration differs between the Lennox (lower NaCl) and Miller (higher NaCl) formulations, which can affect osmotic stress on some strains — confirm which formulation a protocol assumes before substituting.
